fit: olive oil advised in both mixed dietary phases and bowel frequency
assessment: Both randomized-order Mediterranean phases encouraged olive oil with grade and independent consumption unspecified in the inspected body. The same-cohort bowel analysis gives between-phase frequency OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.82–1.28) and similar stool form. The comparison supplies no extra-virgin olive oil-specific effect on Parkinson constipation.

fit: self-reported olive oil and case-control composite diet constipation association
assessment: Fifty-nine Parkinson participants reported cooking with olive oil more often than 54 controls. Within the Parkinson group a higher Mediterranean score was associated with lower constipation odds (unadjusted OR 0.88 per point, 95% CI 0.78–0.98). That model uses the composite score. Oil grade and an oil-specific constipation contrast were not reported.

fit: optional ungraded olive oil and trial-reported anxiety in a different population
assessment: The protocol lists olive oil as a choice within stratified support for older adults with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment. The results abstract reports a favorable SAS direction for the program. The full numeric results, individual exposure and independently assigned oil effect remain unavailable.

fit: shared olive-oil advice and ordinal anxiety change during Parkinson diet phases
assessment: In a local count of the released file, the ketogenic phase had 10 improved, 20 unchanged and four worse anxiety ratings (n=34), and the MCT phase had nine, 22 and six (n=37). These are overlapping crossover phase ratings. Parkinson Anxiety Scale follow-up estimates and a grade-specific olive-oil comparator remain unverified.

fit: self-reported olive oil and composite diet anxiety association in Parkinson disease
assessment: Within 59 Parkinson participants the total Mediterranean score was associated with lower anxiety odds (unadjusted OR 0.88 per point, 95% CI 0.78–0.98). The study did not assign oil or report a pressing-specific olive oil and anxiety estimate.

fit: optional walnut oil and planned depression scale in a non-Parkinson trial
assessment: The program offered walnut oil as a dietary option. The protocol prespecified a geriatric depression scale. Public results material supplies neither the depression comparison nor participant-specific intake, processing grade or oil allocation.

fit: optional peanut oil and planned depression scale in a non-Parkinson trial
assessment: The dietary plan included optional peanut oil and the trial protocol prespecified a geriatric depression scale for the whole program. The refined grade, individual intake, full depression result and oil effect remain unverified.

fit: optional peanut oil within a diabetes support program and reported anxiety
assessment: The 2025 abstract reports a favorable Zung anxiety outcome for combined self-management support. Participants were assigned the support program, with peanut oil a possible dietary choice in the protocol. No cold-pressed preparation, individual intake or oil-specific anxiety result was verified.

fit: shared olive-oil advice and sleep adverse events during Parkinson diet phases
assessment: Table 3 lists mild intermittent insomnia during the ketogenic phase as possibly related to the overall diet. The MCT phase lists a separate serious insomnia and psychosis event after deep brain stimulation, judged unrelated. Phase completion and post-visit counts differ. Olive oil was encouraged in both diets with no isolated effect on insomnia severity.
